summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) Graduate Program is the Korean government's full scholarship for master's and doctoral study in Korea, run by NIIED. It pays airfare, tuition, a monthly living allowance, health insurance and usually one year of Korean language training before the degree. Winners have strong grades (80%+ average), a focused study plan that fits a Korean university, convincing reasons for choosing Korea, and solid references.
lookfor: Strong academic record: cumulative GPA of at least 80% (or the equivalent in the guidelines) at your last school
A clear, realistic study plan that matches your chosen Korean universities and departments
A personal statement showing motivation, background and why Korea
Good references from people who know your academic work
Language readiness (Korean or English scores are a plus) and willingness to learn Korean
Fit with the embassy's or university's priorities (for example fields important to your country)
cycle: The graduate call is published each year around January–February, candidates are nominated in about April, scholars are chosen around June and they enter Korea at the end of August. For 2027 entry, watch for the 2027 GKS Graduate Program notice from January 2027 on Study in Korea and the Korean Embassy in Nigeria website.

eligibility.q: Are you and both of your parents non-Korean citizens (and you do not hold Korean citizenship)?
eligibility.no: GKS is only for foreign nationals whose parents are also foreign nationals.

eligibility.q: Will you be under 40 on 1 September of the selection year?
eligibility.no: You are over the GKS age limit. Consider Commonwealth or university awards without an age cap.

eligibility.q: Will you hold a bachelor's degree (for master's) or master's degree (for PhD) by the date in the guidelines?
eligibility.no: Apply once your degree is completed or will be completed by the stated date.

eligibility.q: Is your cumulative GPA at your last school at least 80% (or the conversion given in the guidelines)?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible this year. A Nigerian Second Class Upper usually converts above 80% but check the official conversion table in the guidelines.

eligibility.q: Have you never studied at a Korean university and never held a GKS award (or can you meet the stated exceptions)?
eligibility.no: Check the exceptions in the current guidelines; otherwise apply to university or KOICA scholarships instead.

eligibility.q: Are you willing to complete one year of Korean language training if required?
eligibility.no: Most scholars take a one-year Korean course first; those with a high TOPIK level may be exempt. If you cannot commit, GKS is not the right fit.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and read the GKS overview
steps.why: GKS rules (age, parents' nationality, GPA) are strict and checked at every stage.
do: Open the Study in Korea GKS invitation page and read the Graduate section.
Check your age on 1 September of the selection year.
Find your cumulative GPA and compare with the 80% rule.
Answer each eligibility question in this guide.
tips: Use a browser translate tool if the page opens in Korean.
avoid: Relying on old blog posts for amounts and dates – they change each year.
check: I meet the age, nationality, degree and GPA rules.

links.t: Study in Korea – GKS invitation programme (official)

steps.title: Choose Embassy track or University track
steps.why: Applicants submit through a Korean mission (embassy) or a Korean university; both nominate candidates to NIIED. Recent guidelines allow only one track per year.
do: Embassy track: you apply through the Korean Embassy in Nigeria and choose universities (recent guidelines: up to 3) – check that Nigeria has an embassy-track quota in the new notice.
University track: you apply directly to one Korean university that has GKS places.
List pros and cons: embassy track lets you choose several universities; university track can be less crowded for some fields.
Decide and write down your track.
tips: Read the country quota table in the new guidelines; it shows how many places each track has for your country.
avoid: Applying through both tracks – recent guidelines disqualify duplicate applications.
check: I know my track and the deadline for it.

links.t: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Nigeria

steps.title: Pick universities and departments
steps.why: Your study plan must match a department that offers your programme (in English or Korean).
do: Open the list of participating universities and departments in the new guidelines.
Find 3 (embassy track) or 1 (university track) programmes that fit your field.
Read each department page: courses, professors, language of instruction.
Optional: email a professor to ask if they accept GKS students in your area.
tips: Mix universities: not all three choices should be the most famous ones (SNU, KAIST, Yonsei, Korea).
avoid: Choosing a department that does not exist in the participating list.
check: My choices are on the official list and fit my plan.

steps.title: Build your timeline
steps.why: The window between the January–February announcement and the deadline is short, and degree confirmation takes weeks.
do: Assume the notice appears in January–February 2027.
Start document requests (transcripts, degree confirmation) in November–December 2026.
Plan drafts of personal statement and study plan in December–January.
Ask referees in January.
tips: Check the Study in Korea notice board and Korean Embassy Abuja site weekly from January.
avoid: Waiting for the notice before ordering transcripts.
check: Key dates are in my calendar.

steps.title: Get transcripts and degree certificates confirmed
steps.why: GKS normally requires degree certificates and transcripts with an apostille or consular confirmation from the Korean Embassy.
do: Request official transcripts and certified copies of your degree certificate from your university.
Check the new guidelines for how to confirm them: apostille (if your country issues it) or consular confirmation at the Korean Embassy in Abuja.
Book an appointment or ask the embassy about consular confirmation fees and time.
Get the GPA conversion document if your scale is not 4.0/4.3/4.5/100.
tips: Ask for extra sealed copies; universities may request originals later.
avoid: Submitting unconfirmed copies – they can be rejected.
check: My transcripts and certificates are confirmed as the guidelines require.

steps.title: Get language scores and other documents
steps.why: TOPIK or English scores are not always mandatory but can earn extra points; you also need passport copies and the official forms.
do: If you have time, take IELTS or TOEFL (or TOPIK if you know Korean); valid scores can earn extra points.
Scan your passport data page (or a national ID if allowed).
Download the official application forms from the new notice.
Prepare a passport photo in the size stated.
tips: Even TOPIK level 1–2 shows commitment; check how scores are counted in the guidelines.
check: I have every document on the checklist.

steps.title: Write the Personal Statement
steps.why: The personal statement shows who you are and why Korea; screeners use it to judge motivation and fit.
steps.prompt: Use the official GKS form: it typically asks about your motivation, background, and plans after study (check the current form).
steps.limit: Use the space or limit given on the official form.
do: Open the official personal statement form in the guidelines.
Write each section in the order asked: motivation, educational background, achievements, future plans.
Give concrete examples and numbers (projects, results, community roles, NYSC).
Explain why Korea specifically: technology, research strength, links to your field.
tips: Write in simple, direct English; reviewers read many forms.
avoid: Generic praise of Korea (K-pop, food) without academic reasons.
check: My statement answers every question on the form.

steps.title: Write the Study Plan
steps.why: The study plan shows what you will study and research and how it fits your chosen department.
steps.prompt: Describe your study goals, study plan in Korea, and future plans (official GKS form; check the current form).
steps.limit: Use the space or limit given on the official form.
do: State your study goal and research area in one short paragraph.
Describe the courses and research topics you will pursue in Korea and why your chosen department fits.
Add the Korean language year to your plan.
End with your plan after graduation and how it benefits your country.
tips: If you apply to 3 universities, make the plan fit all three or adapt per university as allowed.
avoid: A plan that ignores Korean language training.
check: My study plan links my background, Korean programme and future.

steps.title: Get recommendation letters
steps.why: Recent GKS guidelines ask for two recommendation letters, often on the official form and sealed or sent as the notice says.
do: Choose two lecturers or supervisors who know your academic work well.
Give them the official recommendation form, your CV, statement and plan.
Ask for signed letters (sealed if required) and collect them.
Check the notice for how letters must be submitted.
tips: Ask referees to comment on your research potential and character.
avoid: Letters on plain paper when the official form is required.
check: I have two signed letters in the required format.

steps.title: Assemble and submit the application
steps.why: Missing documents or wrong order can disqualify you.
do: Fill the application form; names must match your passport.
Arrange documents in the order stated in the guidelines.
Submit to the Korean Embassy (embassy track) or the university (university track) as instructed.
Keep proof of delivery and a full copy.
tips: Submit a week early to allow for courier delays.
avoid: Using a different document order from the checklist.

steps.title: Prepare for screening and interviews
steps.why: First-round selection by the embassy or university may include an interview; NIIED then reviews and universities assess embassy candidates.
do: Watch your email and phone; respond quickly.
Prepare a 2-minute summary of your study plan.
Practise answers: Why Korea? Why this university? How will you use your degree at home?
Prepare original documents if asked.
tips: Know a few basic Korean greetings – it shows commitment.
check: I can explain my plan clearly in two minutes.

steps.title: Results, medical check and travel
steps.why: Final results come around June; selected scholars then complete medical checks, visa and travel to arrive by late August.
do: Check NIIED/Study in Korea announcements and your email around June.
Complete the medical exam and forms NIIED sends.
Apply for the D-2 student visa at the Korean Embassy.
Follow the airfare and arrival instructions.
tips: Join the GKS scholars' orientation and language institute groups early.
check: I have final selection, visa and travel date.

faq.q: Can I apply through both the embassy and a university?
faq.a: Recent guidelines allow only one track; duplicate applications are disqualified.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Korean?
faq.a: No, but most scholars take a one-year Korean language course first. A TOPIK score can help.
At least 80% cumulative at your last school, or the conversion in the guidelines.
Under 40 on 1 September of the selection year.

faq.q: How much is the monthly allowance?
faq.a: Amounts are set each year in the guidelines; check the current notice for the exact figure.
Usually January–February, with entry to Korea at the end of August.
